name: compute_blast_alignment
description: Compute a local sequence alignment between two biological sequences using the BLAST (Basic Local Alignment Search Tool) algorithm. Returns alignment score, percent identity, e-value, and the aligned regions. Use this tool to assess sequence similarity between two specific sequences (NOT for searching a sequence against a database — use 'blast_search_database' for that).

parameters.name: query_sequence
parameters.description: The first biological sequence to align, as a raw string of single-letter codes (no FASTA header, no whitespace, no line breaks). For proteins use IUPAC amino acid codes (e.g. 'MAEGEIT...'); for nucleotides use A/C/G/T/U. Length must be between 10 and 10000 characters.

parameters.name: subject_sequence
parameters.description: The second biological sequence to align against the query, with the same format requirements as query_sequence (raw single-letter codes, no header, 10-10000 chars). Must be the same molecule type as query_sequence.

parameters.name: sequence_type
parameters.description: The biological molecule type of both sequences. Must be exactly one of: 'protein', 'nucleotide'. This selects the BLAST variant (blastp vs blastn) and the scoring matrix.

parameters.name: evalue_threshold
parameters.description: Maximum e-value threshold for reporting alignments, as a decimal (e.g. 0.001 for stringent, 10.0 for permissive). Alignments with e-value above this threshold are filtered out. Defaults to 10.0 if not specified.

score.description: Raw BLAST alignment score (higher = better alignment).

percent_identity.description: Percent identity of the aligned region (0-100).

evalue.description: Expectation value of the alignment (lower = more significant).

aligned_query.description: Aligned query sequence with gap characters ('-') inserted.

aligned_subject.description: Aligned subject sequence with gap characters ('-') inserted.

return_schema.description: Alignment statistics (score, percent_identity, evalue) and the gapped aligned sequences (aligned_query, aligned_subject).
